text_span.text: "Let us return to your timeline, Laurie,"
"You claimed that during the hour of the storm—the very hour the milk bottle in the study was tampered with—you were in the library, and subsequently the study, accompanied by Miss Talia."
"That is correct, Inspector. We were discussing the family archives. The rain had made us restless."

"There is only one minor complication. I have just spoken with Talia's maid, Winnie. Winnie spent the entire night in the ante-room adjoining Miss Talia's private bedchamber. She is quite adamant that her mistress never left her bed all evening, having taken a mild sedative for her headache at nine o'clock."
"Winnie is a loyal servant, Inspector, but perhaps her own fatigue got the better of her. Or perhaps... she is mistaken about the time."
"Winnie's timepiece is synchronized with the grandfather clock in the hall, which I have just verified,"
"And what of you, Sebastian? Your sudden entrance earlier was... striking. You appeared in the drawing room almost as if by magic."

"I apologize if my arrival startled the household, Inspector. When I heard the glass shatter from the carriage house, I ran back across the courtyard. The mud was thick, and I nearly lost my footing twice, which is why my boots are caked in clay. The side door was bolted, so I had to circle around to the terrace doors. I burst in as quickly as my lungs would allow."
"A breathless run. Yes, that explains the state of your coat, Mr. Whitmore."

"We have a bottle of milk laced with cyanide sitting in a study that was supposed to be empty. We have a young lady asleep in her chambers while her cousin claims her as an alibi. And we have a shattered window with no culprit in sight. Someone in this house is spinning a very delicate web. But webs, gentlemen, are incredibly easy to tear."
